subject: Clarify incident notification timelines & cooperation commitments
messages:
From: Jacob Meyer <jacob.meyer@acmenet.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy_ops@acmenet.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify DPA incident notification timing and cooperation

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Our legal team asked me to confirm the exact breach-notification timeline Redwood will commit to in the DPA. Specifically:

- Do you commit to notifying AcmeNet within 72 hours of becoming aware, or are you comfortable with a 48-hour window for incidents that meet the "personal data exposure" threshold?
- What information will you provide in the initial notice (scope, affected records, mitigation steps)?
- How will Redwood handle cross-border evidence requests and search warrants that may implicate SCCs / DP transfer controls?

Also need assurance that you will preserve forensic evidence and provide a named point of contact available 24x7 during an active incident. Can you share sample contract language and any SOC 2 artifacts you can provide during the diligence?

Best,
Jacob
Senior Counsel, AcmeNet

--
Jacob Meyer
AcmeNet Inc.
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Meyer <jacob.meyer@acmenet.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA incident notification timing and cooperation

Jacob —

Appreciate the clear list. High level answers up front: we can agree to a 72-hour standard notification for reportable breaches, with an option for a 48-hour initial alert for high-severity incidents where we have confirmed personal data exposure and active exploitation. We provide an initial notice with:

- brief summary (what happened, detection time window),
- preliminary scope estimate (systems and records affected),
- immediate mitigation steps and containment status,
- named POC and indications of next steps (forensic timeline).

We will preserve forensic evidence and isolate affected infrastructure; our security team holds forensics snapshots and retains audit logs in read-only archives for the duration required by the DPA. Regarding cross-border or legal process requests, we follow the contractual SCCs and will notify you of requests that implicate customer data transfers; we won’t voluntarily disclose data outside the legal process.

I attached a short redline of proposed DPA language for Section 7 (incident response & cooperation) and a one-page severity matrix we use internally to map response timelines. Laura/Neha — can you review the redline and confirm we can commit to the 48-hour initial alert carve-out and the preservation language?

Jacob — if that sounds workable I can route an updated DPA for your GC to review.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Cloud & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA-Section7-proposed-language-redline.docx, Incident-Notification-severity-matrix.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jacob Meyer <jacob.meyer@acmenet.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 14:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA incident notification timing and cooperation

Rishi / team —

Quick legal review notes:
- Preference from Legal: maintain a 72-hour contractual obligation as the default (aligns with many DPAs and gives us buffer for investigation).
- Approve the 48-hour "initial alert" concept provided it's explicitly labelled as "preliminary notification" and preceded by the phrase "to the extent reasonably practicable" — this reduces strict contractual liability for incomplete facts.
- Redline: add a clause that customer will receive a follow-up substantive report within 30 days (or sooner if containment completes early); we can add exceptions for ongoing criminal/active law enforcement investigations.

On preservation & cooperation: we can commit to preserving forensic snapshots and logs for the longer of (a) regulatory retention period applicable to the customer or (b) 90 days post-incident, unless the customer requests longer in writing. For SCCs: call out that cross-border disclosure will follow the SCCs and any applicable export controls; we will notify customers of legal process requests unless prohibited by law.

I'll add those points to the DPA redline and circulate.

- Laura
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jacob Meyer <jacob.meyer@acmenet.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA incident notification timing and cooperation

Adding technical / ops perspective:

- Detection vs awareness: our telemetry generates automated alerts within minutes, but "awareness" for contractual purposes requires triage by an analyst. That typically adds 4–24 hours depending on time of detection and staffing; we should be explicit in the DPA about the definition of "becoming aware." I propose: "becoming aware" means the time at which Redwood has, following an initial triage, determined that a security event is reasonably likely to have resulted in unauthorized access to personal data.
- Severity matrix (attached) maps: Critical = confirmed exfiltration or active exploitation; High = confirmed exposure but containment in progress; Medium/Low = contained/no evidence of exfiltration.
- For Critical incidents we can commit to an initial 24–48 hour notice window for the initial alert, but we only want to guarantee a substantive report within 30 days. For HIPAA-regulated customers: we will coordinate BA/covered entity obligations and provide required breach reports to support the customer's HIPAA timeline.
- Forensics: we will provide read-only forensic exports and an encrypted evidence container. We require a written request and a defined chain of custody; we will also provide a 24x7 POC during active incidents (rotating on-call schedule).

I'll also attach a stub of the SOC 2 evidence set we can provide for due diligence (redacted).

Neha
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-Forensics-evidence-stub.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Meyer <jacob.meyer@acmenet.com>, Lauren Pike <lauren.pike@acmenet.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Final proposed wording and next steps for DPA Section 7 (Incident Response & Cooperation)

Jacob / Lauren —

Thanks for the thoughtful questions and patience while Legal and SecOps aligned. Attached is the consolidated redline for Section 7. Highlights:

- Notification windows: default contractual obligation = 72 hours after "becoming aware." We include a defined "initial alert" carve-out for high-severity incidents (48 hours for high; 24–48 hours for critical) with the language "to the extent reasonably practicable."
- Definition of "becoming aware" included (initial triage threshold) to avoid ambiguity.
- Forensics & preservation: Redwood will preserve forensic snapshots, audit logs and backups for the longer of the customer's regulatory retention period or 90 days post-incident. Redwood will provide read-only forensic exports under a mutually agreed chain-of-custody process; requests must be accompanied by a written evidence request form.
- Cross-border & legal process: Redwood will comply with SCCs for transfers and will notify the customer of compelled disclosures unless prohibited. We will evaluate law enforcement requests and seek to scope disclosures narrowly.
- HIPAA customers: we will provide reasonable cooperation for the customer's HIPAA reporting obligations and supply the necessary technical details for any 60/90-day windows as required by the customer.

If those points are acceptable, please let me know and we can circulate a DPA with the final redline for your GC to sign. Alternatively, if you prefer a clause-level call with Laura for one focused hour we can schedule next week.

Thanks — appreciate moving this to a final form.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Cloud & Compliance
Redwood Inference
